oslo-norway-scenic-roads-trollstigen-and.slogan: A 245 km loop out of Trollstigen and Geiranger Expedition
oslo-norway-scenic-roads-trollstigen-and.story: A proper escape from Oslo with roads worth waking up for. 245 km round from Åneby - plan on about 5 h 07 of riding. The stops in between: Scenic stretch near Kløfta, near Ås and Kolbotn. near Flateby is the high point. The line favours views over speed.

oslo-norway-scenic-roads-trollstigen-and.speedBand: 50–80 km/h riding core, local limits always win

sections.advice: This Scenic stretch near Kløfta → High point near Flateby stretch is for rhythm and scenery. Keep your head up, let the view breathe, and resist turning every open bend into a target. Stop once properly rather than half-stopping everywhere.

Photo stop near Ås → Near Kolbotn is the technical section. Hairpins, gradients and mixed traffic can stack up quickly; use low drama inputs, stay wide of centre lines and expect buses or riders appearing exactly where optimism says they will not.

waypoints.name: Stelvio Pass summit
waypoints.advice: 2757 m, and the road stops climbing. The road climbs 1532 m on the way up to it, steadily. Nothing on this route is higher. At this height the road is a summer one: snow gates can stay shut into June and shut again in October. Next is Prato allo Stelvio, mostly downhill.

waypoints.name: Santa Maria Val Müstair
waypoints.advice: Fill up here — 74 km left and no pump marked after this. Next is Umbrail Pass, climbing 1126 m.

waypoints.name: Umbrail Pass
waypoints.advice: You top out at 2501 m here. The road climbs 1126 m on the way up to it, steadily. Next is Back to Bormio, mostly downhill.

waypoints.name: Back to Bormio
waypoints.advice: Back to Bormio closes the day. You lose 1276 m on the way down to it, steadily.

scenicChapters.title: Stelvio Pass
scenicChapters.narrative: For 44 km this is Stelvio Pass, a road with a name of its own and a reason for it. Expect company on a summer weekend. Early is better than fast.
scenicChapters.riderNote: Check the pass is open before you commit to it.

scenicChapters.title: Stelvio Pass
scenicChapters.narrative: First and second gear more often than not. Look through each corner to the next one and let the engine do the holding. The valley floor is behind you and the road starts working for its height at about 122.5%. Corners stack above one another where the ground allows nothing straighter.
scenicChapters.riderNote: Check the pass is open before you commit to it.

scenicChapters.title: Stelvio Pass
scenicChapters.narrative: The last of the trees go and the road runs out onto open ground. The summit sits at 2757 m, and what surrounds it is rock, weather and distance — cold comes early up here and stays late. Ride it with something in reserve: the summit is not the end of the work, only the middle of it.
scenicChapters.riderNote: Check the pass is open before you commit to it.

milan-stelvio-and-gavia-serious-pass-day.story: A 445 km loop that starts and ends near Bormio, about 8 h 34 of riding. It goes by way of Santa Maria and Tirano. The climbs: Stelvio Pass, Gavia Pass, Stelvio Pass summit and Umbrail Pass. It tops out at about 2,750 m. Stelvio Pass and Gavia Pass are open in summer only - check it is open before you set off. It crosses from Italy into Switzerland - carry ID and check vignette or toll rules. The passes are the reason to go.

scenicChapters.title: Bainskloof Pass
scenicChapters.narrative: Expect company on a summer weekend. Early is better than fast. For 17 km this is Bainskloof Pass, a road with a name of its own and a reason for it.
